title: Gestures, Touch Events & Mobile ARIA ⚡
description: Design touch interactions that are accessible, provide alternatives to complex gestures, and use mobile‑aware ARIA.

slides.title: Beyond Tap: Swipes, Pinches & Long‑press 🤏
slides.content:
Touchscreens enable rich gestures: swipe, pinch‑zoom, drag, long‑press. However, these can be inaccessible to:

- Users with motor disabilities who can't perform precise multi‑finger gestures.
- Blind users who rely on screen reader gestures (which use the same swipes).
- Switch users who have only binary input.

WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures: If a multi‑point or path‑based gesture is required, provide a single‑pointer alternative (e.g., swipe to delete → also add a Delete button).

quizData.question: An app uses a pinch gesture to zoom. What is required to meet WCAG 2.5.1?

options.text: Nothing, pinch is a standard gesture
Provide + and – buttons as an alternative

quizData.explanation: Multi‑point gestures must have a single‑pointer or keyboard equivalent.

slides.title: Pointer Cancellation & Touch Events 🖐️
slides.content:
WCAG 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation: Functions must not be triggered on the down‑event of a pointer unless the user can undo or abort.

- Use `click` event instead of `mousedown`/`touchstart` for actions.
- For custom touch interactions, use `pointerup` and allow the user to drag their finger away to cancel.

This prevents accidental activation on touchscreens.

slides.title: Safe Touch Event Pattern

quizData.question: Why is it recommended to use 'click' instead of 'touchstart' for button actions?

options.text: It allows the user to abort by moving their finger away before releasing

quizData.explanation: Click fires on pointer up, allowing cancellation by sliding off the target.

slides.title: Mobile ARIA & Role 'Application' ⚠️
slides.content:
On mobile, some ARIA patterns work differently:

- `role="application"` should be avoided on mobile – it takes over all gesture handling and can confuse screen reader users.
- `aria‑haspopup` and `aria‑expanded` are crucial for dropdowns and menus.
- `aria‑live` regions may not announce content if focus is elsewhere; on mobile, consider moving focus to the dynamic content to ensure announcement.
- Use native mobile patterns where possible (e.g., native selects) – they already work well with assistive tech.

slides.title: Accessible Drag‑and‑Drop 🖱️
slides.content:
Drag‑and‑drop is inherently inaccessible without a mouse. To make it accessible:

- Add keyboard controls: arrow keys to move items, Enter/Space to pick up and drop.
- Use `aria‑grabbed` and `aria‑dropeffect` (though ARIA 1.2 may deprecate these, check).
- Provide a non‑drag alternative (e.g., a 'Move to...' button with a dropdown).
- Ensure focus management during the operation.

Libraries like `react‑beautiful‑dnd` have accessibility add‑ons.

quizData.question: A task list reordering only works by dragging items. How do you make it accessible?

options.text: Provide keyboard controls and a non‑drag method (e.g., up/down buttons per item)

quizData.explanation: Keyboard and alternative interaction must be provided to meet WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test with Screen Curtain
On iOS, triple‑tap with three fingers while VoiceOver is on. Your screen goes black. Now try to use your site. If you can't, it's not accessible.
